method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Through the information-architecture and cognitive-ergonomics lens this product is visibly the work of people who think about naming — the board's plain-language column definitions, Timeline's 'Anyone holding the link can read it', the Notes/Tasks provenance loop that reads correctly from both ends, and the landing page's NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE line are all above the standard of most shipping software. What holds every surface below the 9.5 floor is the same class of defect repeated: taxonomies that are almost right and then break. 'Projects' scoping Home, Inbox and My work; a task detail rail where two of seven 'fields' are actions; three status vocabularies across three products where Timeline's 'Complete' and Tasks' 'Done' mean the same thing; three unreconciled countdowns for one wedding ('Day 11 of 97', '79 days to go', 'in 16 days'); a pricing page whose four ways in are half named and half described. The second pattern is mobile losing structure rather than adapting it — dropped counts in Notes, a dropped sort control, a dropped project level in Timeline, and a task detail that files identity below the conversation composer — set against Timeline's vertical spine and About's mobile layout, which prove the team can re-think for narrow screens when it chooses to. Two things I could not judge and have not credited: nothing here reveals motion, drag, filter behaviour, or focus order, and the marketing captures are single viewports, so section-level hierarchy below the fold is unassessed on all three pages. No surface warrants a veto; the clipped priority column in the Tasks list ('Hig'/'Low'/'No' at 1440) is the closest thing to an embarrassment and is still only a table that needs to fit.

surfaces.rationale: The board's plain-language column definitions are the best IA in the whole set: 'Agreed and ready to start.', 'In motion right now.', 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.' teach the workflow without a manual, and 'Nothing held up' beats a generic empty state. Against that sit real structural faults. The sidebar heading 'Projects' scopes three things that are not projects (Home, Inbox 8, My work) before a second heading 'Project folders' introduces the actual project, and 'Home' also exists as an unlabelled house glyph at the top of the icon rail — one destination, two entry points, filed under the wrong noun. In the desktop list view at 1440 the priority column is clipped mid-word: the header reads 'P' and the values read 'Hig', 'Low', 'No', with no visible horizontal-scroll affordance. That same list triple-encodes state — group header 'To do', a status circle, and a STATUS cell all saying the same thing on every row — while the OWNER column reads 'Orla' on all thirteen rows and carries no information for ~180px, and the DATES column mixes 'Unscheduled', 'Milestone · 1 Aug', 'Due 16 Jul' and 'Done', the last of which is a completion state occupying a date field. The header chip 'Planning 5 undated' never says what Planning is, and 'Day 11 of 97' names no anchor — it also fails to reconcile with Timeline's '79 days to go' for the same wedding. On mobile six stacked bands of chrome (title, counters, Board/List/Schedule/Calendar, Filter/Sort/Display, a column-name chip row, the column header) consume roughly 330px of an 844px viewport before the first card, and the bottom tab bar mixes a view switcher ('Board ⌄') in among four destinations while duplicating the view tabs already on screen. Card tags apply one grey chip treatment to semantically different things — 'Mara & Finn' (people) next to 'Venue', 'Bar', 'Enquiry' (categories). Static captures cannot show drag, column collapse, or filter behaviour, so I have credited none of it.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rename the sidebar's first group so Home, Inbox and My work are not filed under 'Projects', and make the list view's priority column survive a 1440 viewport instead of clipping to 'Hig'/'Low'/'No' — the two defects that make a considered board read as unfinished.

surfaces.rationale: The control row is well chosen: status, owner, due date, priority and 'Mark done' are the five things you actually change, promoted out of the field stack and sitting directly under the title, with a 'The Orchard, events / T-1' breadcrumb giving location. The SOURCE block is the strongest single idea here — 'From Notes · open source' plus the quoted approved wording, 'Confirm marquee sides with hire company before Thursday', makes the Notes-to-Tasks provenance legible rather than implied. But the right rail is a flat unordered stack of seven small-caps labels with no grouping: REPEATS (scheduling), TAGS (classification), CONTACT (people), PROJECT (location), SOURCE (provenance), COPIES and ADD FIELD. Two of those seven are not fields at all — COPIES holds a 'Make copies' button and ADD FIELD offers exactly one option, '+ Amount' — so the label pattern the eye is trying to learn breaks twice. 'COPIES / Make copies' names nothing a non-technical reader can decode, which is conspicuous next to the board's carefully explained columns. PROJECT restates 'The Orchard, events' already shown in the breadcrumb of the same modal. The worst cost is on mobile: the entire right rail is appended below the CONVERSATION section, so REPEATS, TAGS and CONTACT come after description, subtasks, resources, the empty-conversation notice and the reply composer — the metadata that identifies the task is last, and the capture cuts off mid-'CONTACT' at the fold. Someone checking on a phone which project a task belongs to or who the contact is must scroll past everything else. The keyboard hint 'Press e to open a task full-screen, and j or k to move between tasks.' sits inside the content column where conversation belongs rather than in chrome. No dialog focus behaviour, escape handling or field-editing flow is observable from a still.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Reorder the mobile sheet so identity and context (project, contact, tags, source) sit directly under the control row rather than below the conversation composer, and split the desktop right rail into a labelled field group and a separate actions group so COPIES and ADD FIELD stop masquerading as fields.

surfaces.rationale: The strongest information architecture of the four app surfaces. The tab triad 'Notebook 14 / Review 8 / In Tasks 6' names a triage state rather than a folder, the capture box sits above everything else so the product's primary job is the first thing on screen, and the per-item glyphs (document, microphone, image) encode capture type quietly without a legend. The contextual verbs 'Keep', 'Turn into task', 'Delete' appear only on 'To review' items and are all plain English. The detail footer — 'Captured 35 minutes ago', 'Edited 31 minutes ago', and 'In Tasks: Confirm marquee sides with hire company before Thursday' as a live link — closes the provenance loop that the task detail opens, and that bidirectional legibility is the best cross-product idea in the evidence. The gaps are all about how much the reader must infer. Nothing states that Notebook is the superset and Review and In Tasks are subsets, so the counts 14/8/6 can equally be read as three parallel buckets totalling 28. Two unrelated filtering mechanisms stack — the tab row, then an 'All notes ⌄' dropdown, then search — with no stated relationship between the tabs and the dropdown. 'Private to you' sits centred in the header between the tabs and a '…', so its scope is ambiguous: the notebook, or the selected note. The detail pane leaves roughly 350px of white between three lines of note text and a bottom-anchored metadata footer, detaching the provenance from what it describes. Mobile drops the tab counts — the useful half of those labels — clips the 'Notebook' tab highlight off the left edge, and silently removes the 'Newest first' sort control, so ordering cannot be changed on a phone. Row heights alternate between roughly 100px and 150px depending on whether triage actions are present, which breaks the scan rhythm.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Make the Notebook/Review/In Tasks relationship explicit — show Review and In Tasks as subsets of the Notebook count rather than three equal-weight tabs — and carry the counts through to mobile, where they are dropped.

surfaces.rationale: 'Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.' is the best naming decision anywhere in this review: it states the sharing state in a sentence a non-technical person can act on, with no public/unlisted/permissions jargon. The alternating above/below milestone labels along the axis work, 'Today' is marked on the rail, and the mobile view genuinely rethinks the timeline as a vertical spine rather than squeezing the horizontal one — a considered responsive decision, not a fallback. The costs are duplication and vocabulary. '3 Oct' and the 79-day count appear both in the top chrome ('Wedding day · 3 Oct · 79 days to go') and again in the hero stat block, inside one viewport. That stat block also files '2 of 9 complete' — milestone progress — under a countdown headed 'Until wedding day / 79 / days', where it does not belong. The timeline introduces a fourth status vocabulary across the suite: 'Complete', 'Our next milestone', 'Coming up', 'Later' — where 'Complete' means what Tasks calls 'Done', and no rule on screen explains why 8 Aug is 'Coming up' but 3 Oct is 'Later'. Combined with Tasks' 'Day 11 of 97' and this page's 'in 16 days', a user tracking one wedding is holding three unreconciled countdowns. The '4 milestones' bracket under a run of hollow dots does not clearly bound which dots it collapses — I count seven hollow dots and a bracket spanning roughly three of them. The control row puts three different kinds of thing side by side: Timeline/Milestones is a view segment, Preview is a mode with an unstated audience, Share is an action, and Preview and Share are styled as siblings. Mobile drops 'The Orchard, events' entirely, losing a level of hierarchy, and its bottom tab bar has four items where Tasks has five — the nav shape changes between products.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Reconcile the countdown and status language with Tasks — one anchor for 'how long until the day', and 'Complete' matching Tasks' 'Done' — and state the rule that separates 'Coming up' from 'Later' instead of leaving the reader to infer it.

surfaces.rationale: 'Project management for people outside tech.' is the clearest positioning statement in the evidence set, and colouring only 'outside' puts the emphasis exactly on the word carrying the argument. The subhead names all three products in their first sentence — 'Notes, Tasks and Timeline. One calm system for people with work to manage, not software to manage.' — so the vocabulary is seeded before the reader meets it anywhere else. The mono line 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' is superb IA compression: two arrows teach the whole mental model of the suite. The two CTAs are correctly differentiated by commitment and their arrows encode destination type — a down arrow on 'See the system at work' meaning scroll, a right arrow on 'Join the waitlist' meaning go. Three faults through my lens. First, that mono flow line — structurally the most important element on the page — is set at roughly 11px in grey, quieter than everything around it, so the model it teaches is the easiest thing to miss. Second, the nav hides all three products behind a 'Products ⌄' dropdown, so a first-time reader is handed three product names in the subhead and finds none of them in the navigation. Third, 'Design' as a top-level item beside Pricing and About is the least self-explaining label in the bar, and for an audience explicitly defined as people outside tech it is the one word that will not resolve on sight. On mobile the headline holds at four lines, CTAs stack full width, and the next section eyebrow 'ONE THREAD, THROUGH THE STUDIO' is already visible — so mobile actually communicates that the page continues, while desktop leaves roughly 200px of dead space and no scroll cue. Mobile also shows a promoted 'Products ⌄' next to a hamburger, two nav mechanisms whose division of contents is not guessable. The evidence is one viewport per breakpoint, so I can judge nothing about the section hierarchy below the fold and have credited none of it.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Give 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' the visual weight its structural job deserves and surface the three product names in the nav rather than burying them under a 'Products' dropdown the subhead has already contradicted.

surfaces.rationale: The thesis hierarchy is right — eyebrow 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER' with a violet node on a vertical rule, then a four-line headline that states the whole argument, 'Project management software was built by tech companies, for tech companies.' The rule running down the left is a good structural device, telling you this is one continuous argument rather than a set of blocks, and the small hollow node visible on mobile where the next beat begins echoes Timeline's milestone dots — a real cross-surface motif rather than decoration. Body measure is well judged at roughly 60-65 characters. The desktop layout, though, spends half its viewport and shows less than mobile does. The body paragraph starts at x≈733 while the headline starts at x≈122, leaving a roughly 600px empty column between the spine and the text and forcing a long horizontal jump with nothing bridging it — it reads as a two-column layout with its left column missing. Because of that, the desktop first viewport contains only the thesis and one paragraph; the mobile capture at the same scroll position already shows the argument's hinge, the bolded 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way.', and the start of the next beat, 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages.' The narrow screen is doing a better job of revealing structure than the wide one, which inverts the usual relationship. Separately, one page carries three names: the nav says 'About', the eyebrow says 'A NOTE FROM THE FOUNDER', and the document title in capture-results.json is 'Founder's Note · Signal Studio'. Someone who remembers the founder's note will look for it and find 'About'. Only the first viewport was captured, so I cannot assess how the spine carries the rest of the argument.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Close the empty left column on desktop so the body sits in a readable relationship to the headline and the argument's hinge line reaches the first viewport, as it already does on mobile.

surfaces.rationale: 'One clear system. Four ways in.' is exactly the right headline for a pricing page — it hands the reader the count before the options appear, so they know how many things they are about to compare. The subhead then orders all four against situations rather than feature lists: 'Start free, pay less while studying, move to Pro for ongoing work, or shape an Enterprise start with Ethan.' Putting the terms strip ('No charge / on the waitlist', 'VAT included / at the prevailing rate', 'Terms repeated / before purchase') above the tiers is a considered inversion — you learn the ground rules before you compare — and the second section header names its comparison axes in advance: 'Compare the price, workspace limit and the terms settled today.' Three axes is a schema a reader can hold. The faults are naming and burial. The subhead's four items are two proper names (Pro, Enterprise) and two situations (start free, pay less while studying), so when the reader meets four named cards below they must re-map half the list. 'Ethan' appears with no antecedent — this page never says who he is; that is established on About, which a pricing visitor may not have read. Most significantly, 'No charge on the waitlist' means the product cannot currently be bought, which is the single most consequential fact on a pricing page, and it sits in roughly 13px grey inside a band rather than in the hierarchy's top level. No price appears in the first viewport at either breakpoint — desktop spends the hero on a headline, a subhead, roughly 170px of gap and the strip, then opens a second full section header before any number. Two screens of preamble on the page people arrive at for numbers. The desktop hero also leaves everything right of x≈830 empty, the same unfilled right column as About. Mobile handles the strip better, stacking it as a ruled list, and its first screen is measurably denser and better used than desktop's.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Raise the fact that nothing is purchasable yet out of the grey terms strip into the page's primary hierarchy, and use consistent tier names in the subhead so the reader is not re-mapping two descriptions onto two names when the cards appear.
